quick.summary: Why code tests miss the errors that happen right on the boundaries.
quick.takeaway: Test the exact breaking point of your code, not just the normal cases.

beats.line: The pipeline broke on negative numbers today. Why did our test pass?
Think of a bridge with a weight limit.
The sign says maximum five tons.
So you drive a four ton truck across to check?
Yes. But a real test drives exactly five tons across.
And then you test five tons and a feather.
Oh. We only tested positive numbers in the middle.
Right. We call this boundary value analysis.
Can I just say testing the edge?
Testing the edge. The bugs hide right on the line.
Next time I will test the exact breaking point.
That is how you build a sturdy bridge.

quiz.question: Which value is most important to include in your code tests?
options: The exact boundary where the system behavior changes.
A completely random number chosen by a generator.
A number sitting safely in the middle of your range.
A value that proves your background configuration is correct.
quiz.explanation: Bugs frequently happen exactly on the dividing line between valid and invalid data.

quiz.question: If your code works for a normal case, it will naturally handle the edge cases.
quiz.explanation: Normal cases do not test how the code handles limits, zero values, or sudden transitions.
